rules_text:
Rules summary Contents 1 Overview 2 Actions 3 Your Monkey 4 Game End 5 Scoring Overview Score points by managing your monkey's movements and complete (gain) pumpkin cards and bonus card to win. Top row of cards: Capybara cards Bottom row of cards: Pumpkin cards Actions You can do one of three actions on your turn: 1. Move monkey forward to gain capybara cards a. Move monkey forward 1 space to gain 1 card; or b. Move monkey forward 3 spaces to gain 2 cards; or c. Move monkey forward 5 spaces to gain 3 cards. Cards picked up can be inserted anywhere BEHIND where you monkey is. It is important to keep in mind that the 2 cards you take do not need to be next to each other on the table. They do, however, need to be inserted in the same spot in your line of capybaras in any order you prefer. 2. Move monkey forward to gain pumpkin cards You can claim a private or on display pumpkin cards when you have all the required capybaras. You can also substitute a requirement by moving the monkey forward 3 more steps. Note that the one private pumpkin card you picked at the beginning will not be replaced once it is completed. "Gaining" a pumpkin card means completing one. It is important to keep in mind that in order to gain (complete) a pumpkin card, your monkey will need to move OVER all of the cards required. Meaning, you must start your monkey to the RIGHT of the first card that you will need in order to achieve this. Cards required to complete a pumpkin card do not need to be in any specific orders. You just need to have the required quantity. You may forgo any Capybara condition by moving forward 3 steps. Your Monkey Monkey's Movement Monkey's movement is the key to this game. Moving the monkey forward allows you to gain capybara cards or pumpkin cards. You will need to move your monkey back once it reaches the end of the line in order to perform more actions. The monkey's maximum movement is 3 at the start of the game. Growing your Monkey When you complete your private pumpkin card OR 3 pumpkin cards on display, your monkey will grow and its maximum movement will increase to 4. This is the monkey's maximum movement for the game. Game End Game end when one of these 2 conditions are met: 1. One player claimed 5 pumpkins 2. Capybara deck is empty AND there are only 4 cards left on display Scoring Sum all the scores on the pumpkin cards that you have collected; and Sum the points you've earned from the bonus card.

[Rating: 1/10] I was expecting a children's game, then was disappointed when I slowly realized it's a train game in disguise. A minimalist train game about managing the line of cars. And the capybaras make it way less intuitive than normal. Even when I finally grasped it, it was a ton of busywork moving the monkey backwards to DO anything.

[Rating: 2/10] Ohhhh boy. And I love capybaras, too. I so hope this game gets a remake with either rules or rules translation to English that make more sense and create a good challenge/variability to the game. I think the possibility is there because the game was created by a VERY excellent & talented designer.

[Rating: 2/10] Drafting sets to score goal cards, with the constraint that you have a moving pointer where collected cards go on one side and goals are scored using the other (the pointer moving left every time you claim cards, with turns being skipped to drag it back). Nothing very interesting happening, though, and the theme didn't seem to connect to the gameplay at all.

[Rating: 3/10] What an unfortunately tedious game, having to constantly move your monkey forward and back to gain cards and fulfill objectives, any planning you might be able to do is often left to luck because the new pumpkin card won’t necessarily be in a pattern you’ve already constructed.  Furthermore, I am at a loss why the star/dark blue/E cards are not qualified for some of the bonus cards (namely the one type and all types), they are also capybara but for no good reason are left out, so if I started out with them I get a disadvantage compared to other people?

[Rating: 3/10] Played on BGA.  Really weird theme.  Abstract beyond all, with weird actions that never feel efficient.

[Rating: 3.8/10] set collection and contract fulfilling game seems nothing special from other games
